description:
Goal
Make the shared Enum.reduce* bridge callable's surface/return type a convergent, identity-correlated fixed point, so it behaves identically across List, Range, and Map. This is the ROOT defect behind the reduce cluster: fz-bfh.1, fz-bfh.2, fz-bfh.3, and the range+map convergence storm fz-bfh.4. Fix it here once; those are its regression targets.

Root (proven by bisection + telemetry)
Public Enum.reduce/2,3 and reduce_while/3 wrap the user reducer in a bridge closure `fn(entry, inner_acc) -> {:cont, reducer.(entry, inner_acc)} end` that CAPTURES the reducer (a callable) and dispatches Enumerable.reduce*. Two coupled problems:

1. Positional capture-prefix correlation. The captured callable's flow-fact / publication boundary is correlated POSITIONALLY against the enclosing executable's input layout. Non-List impls thread the reducer behind a run of scalar collection-state lanes (Range: reduce_cont(first,last,step,current,acc,reducer); Map: reduce_while_cont(map,count,index,acc,reducer)); List has a single heap-ref prefix (reduce_cont(list,acc,reducer)). The scalar lead-prefix shifts the position, decorrelating the callable from its boundary.

2. Non-monotone surface join. When more than one non-List shape reaches the shared bridge, the activation/return-type fixpoint does not converge.

Discriminating evidence (release fz2, interp):
- Capture TYPE is the discriminator: a non-callable (int) capture through Range works; a CALLABLE capture through Range fails. Matrix (none/int capture: List/Range/Map all pass; callable capture: List passes, Range and Map both fail).
- Map's Enumerable.reduce works fine with a non-capturing reducer; only the captured-callable bridge breaks it. So it is not a Map-reduce bug.
- Convergence trigger is two DISTINCT non-List shapes meeting the bridge: range+range, list+list, range+list, map+list all converge in <0.1s; range+map storms (~281k jobs, 15s drive-limit). Telemetry: activation_analysis.defined ~52941, paired 1:1 with return_type.defined; top-20 functions = 96% of re-analyses; #1 oscillator is Enum.reduce (fn69); a churning callsite targets the Map reduce fn with return_ty: None on Ty(19) inputs (the same fn/type as fz-bfh.3's absent value).

One instability, two faces: with one non-List shape + captured callable it settles to a WRONG bottom (return_ty None -> absent value / empty or multiple boundaries / lane miscount = the crashes fz-bfh.1/.2/.3); with two non-List shapes it NEVER settles (= the storm fz-bfh.4).

Required work
- Correlate the captured callable's boundary/flow by callable IDENTITY: a single published fact minted at the producer and threaded through transport, not re-derived from capture-prefix position at each consumer. ShapeId stays pure layout; the callable contract must not be fused into surrounding lane position.
- Make the bridge callable's surface/return-type analysis a monotone, convergent join across protocol surfaces, so multiple non-List shapes settle to one fixed point instead of oscillating.
- Keep the fix generic across the shared Enum.reduce* bridge; do not special-case Range, Map, or any Enum helper. Remove the fz-bin.16 bridge-avoidance scaffold in take/drop/split only once the generic fix makes it unnecessary.

Checks
- All regression targets turn green on interp + run + build: fz-bfh.1, fz-bfh.2, fz-bfh.3, fz-bfh.4.
- enum_tier0 (reduce/2,3,reduce_while over List+Range+Map) neither storms nor crashes once re-enabled.
- enum_take_drop_split, range_enumerable, map_enumerable remain green.
- cargo test --lib and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings.

comments.text: During fz-bin.16, the original native lowering fatal was traced to direct callable reducer captures flowing through the shared Enum.reduce/3 bridge. The fz-bin.16 runtime path avoids that bridge for take/drop/split, but the generic compiler issue remains: shared bridge callable captures need correlated direct callable shapes instead of falling back to generic callable inputs that native tries to box without a boundary.

fz-bfh.1 is a hard-crash manifestation of this same shared Enum.reduce/3 bridge capture-correlation gap, reproduced minimally over a Range with a scalar accumulator (fails interp/run/build with zero fixture coverage). The generic fix here likely subsumes fz-bfh.1; coordinate so one correlation fix closes both rather than two local patches.

Cluster surfaced via enum_tier0 honest-coverage extension (reduce/2,3,reduce_while over Range+Map): fz-bfh.2 (multi-surface settled_callable_boundary error: reduce/2-over-Range, reduce_while-over-Map) and fz-bfh.3 (Map reduce materializes absent value). All share this shared-reduce-bridge capture-correlation root; one generic publication/correlation fix should cover fz-bfh.1/.2/.3 and this.

title: Root: shared Enum.reduce* bridge callable surface is not a convergent, identity-correlated fixed point over non-List Enumerables
